To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the yield of rice is positively correlated with its protein content and protein yield.

1) the yield, yield attributing traits and nutritional traits are positively correlated with each other and 2) the yield and yield attributing traits are more strongly correlated than the nutritional traits.

the genetic variation of yield and yield components is high and the correlation between the traits is low, which indicates that selection for yield can be done without affecting other characters and that the correlation between yield components is not high enough to be ignored in selection.

the genetic control of yield, quality and other characters and the relationship between them in rice.
understanding the genetic architecture of rice grain quality traits and their relationship to grain yield.
understanding the genetic control of the complex traits in rice and to develop a better understanding of the genetic basis of these traits.

, the grain yield is the most important character in rice, and the other characters like plant height, panicle number, panicle length, grain number, 1000-grain weight, and harvest index have significant and positive correlation with grain yield.
, in the present study the highest positive correlation was found between yield attributing traits and grain yield.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were able to establish significant positive and negative correlations between yield, quality, its components and other traits in rice and that these relationships can be used in selection for the improvement of rice.
the correlation analysis of the characters under study revealed a positive correlation between grain yield, plant height and panicle length, grain length, grain breadth and 100-grain weight.
the yield of rice is positively associated with plant height and panicle length, and negatively correlated with number of tillers per plant.

we have shown that the yield and yield components are highly correlated with the micronutrient contents in rice.
the yield of a rice plant depends on the interaction between its height, number of panicles per hill, number of grains per panicle and grain weight.
